parsed.explanation: Local state law is strongly protective and operating in facilities, services, courts and care, but the combined regime retains systemic federal exposures: entry screening for document discrepancy with possible refusal and lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal facility exclusion, and documented severe abuse in federal immigration custody. State protections do not cancel federal border, facility or detention actors. Minors face added national care and school pressure and unresolved local ballot measures. This is below the 0.65 anchors, which lack a comparable national screening/facility/custody layer, and above 0.45, because in-state facilities, street recourse and state custody have documented working remedies.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal cable requires refusal and additional evidence where documents/records cast reasonable doubt on sex; suspected wilful misrepresentation may be considered for permanent fraud ineligibility, though not automatic. X passports are no longer newly issued, existing valid until expiration; travellers report confiscation/blocking abroad.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, limited waivers exist, and passport policy is challenged in courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger investigation, refusal or detention, moving the traveller from entry screening into federal custody exposure that state protections do not control.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men. Federal corrections adopted a model removing hormone medication and imposing short haircuts and psychiatric substitution; reporting on transgender prisoners stopped from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State custody relief is documented: 2024 consent decree expands healthcare and creates voluntary specialised housing, with compensation, after a 2019 class action over sexual/physical violence and denied care.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State consent-decree protections do not govern federal immigration or federal corrections custody; detention pathway determines which regime applies.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity. Some states ban facilities, but this state is not documented among them; national order remains a federal-building exposure.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State civil-rights ruling in 2013 and 2023 law grant full bathroom access; anti-discrimination law covers public accommodations since 2008, expanded in 2025.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facility protection operates for state/private facilities, while federal buildings and agencies follow the national restriction unless enjoined.

care_services.exposure: National orders target youth gender-affirming care and funding; a national rule blocks public insurance funds for care under 18/19, causing the state to suspend youth public coverage from 13 October 2026. Hospital compliance with the May 2026 court order is not documented.
care_services.protection: State shield law guarantees gender-affirming care and safe passage; insurance must cover reassignment surgery; May 2026 highest court ordered a hospital to resume puberty blockers and hormone therapy after finding discrimination.
care_services.interaction: State care protection is constrained by national funding conditions; adult visitor care is not documented as banned, but minor traveller care and continuity remain uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National policy defines sex as binary at birth, removes gender-identity materials and pronoun policies, bans trans athletes, and counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; cash-reward guidance uses radical gender ideology framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Employment discrimination based on gender identity is prohibited nationally under 2020 ruling; gender-identity hate crimes are punishable nationally; several national orders have been blocked or enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises outing and enforcement risk at federal level, while state courts and anti-discrimination law provide countervailing recourse locally.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders direct investigation of schools for gender ideology and criminal prosecution related to facilitating social transition; youth care funding is restricted nationally. District-level bans on transgender students in sex-aligned sports are documented, and November 2026 ballot measures would add statewide sports and surgery restrictions if passed.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-discrimination act requires chosen names/pronouns in schools, bans deadnaming/misgendering, allows any uniform option, protects youth care at state level, and conversion therapy for minors is banned.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor traveller is not governed by resident school or public-insurance rules in the same way, but district sports policies, hospital practice and national funding pressure create documented uncertainty for care and participation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific trans killing or violence rate against the general homicide baseline is documented. National polling shows majority support for assigned-sex documents and sports restrictions, indicating scepticism, but not documented routine street targeting in this state.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime law covers gender identity/expression since 2001 with enhancements; 2009 first-degree murder conviction with hate-crime finding; gay-panic defence abolished in 2020; anti-bullying law covers gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State police and courts have documented capacity to prosecute bias violence, partially mediating national hostile framing for street-level encounters.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Key uncertainties remain: whether ballot measures pass, hospital compliance with resumed care, operating status of 2025 document provisions after 1 October 2026, and which national orders remain enjoined at travel time.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Working state remedies are documented through courts, consent decree, anti-discrimination enforcement and the 2026 hospital ruling; national litigation over passports and executive orders is active.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are regime-specific; state relief does not remedy federal entry refusal, federal custody abuse or federal facility exclusion.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-C because ongoing police extortion and overnight detention of visitors is not documented in this state, and state courts, hate-crime enforcement and a consent decree provide operating recourse absent there. Federal custody abuse is severe but is not shown as routine street-level targeting of visitors in the state.

Similar to 0.55-E in having recurring border friction and partially effective remedies, but lower because the border rule is a national cable system with refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, plus documented federal custody abuse and a federal facility bar, rather than one airport practice partly disciplined.

Lower than 0.75-C because that anchor has no active trans-facing border or facility restriction and no documented federal custody campaign. Here state protections are stronger, but the combined regime adds national entry screening, federal facilities exclusion and severe federal custody reports that the anchor lacks.

parsed.synthesis: In-state, a trans visitor encounters unusually strong operating protections: full facility access, enforceable anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, protective custody decree and court-ordered care. Those protections materially raise safety within the state. The combined regime, however, is not reducible to the state: arrival, federal buildings and any federal detention are governed by a binary national document regime, discrepancy-based refusal and fraud screening, facility exclusion and documented abusive custody. That federal layer, plus national pressure on minors' care and unresolved ballot measures, prevents a reduced-risk rating despite strong local protections.
